b38759ef3b3523d3c3d76d49e7440f26a3c14883.summary: Malpedia entry for ZXShell, a backdoor also known as Sensocode. Per FireEye it can be downloaded from the internet, particularly from Chinese hacker websites. It can scan ports, log keystrokes, capture screenshots, open proxies, run reverse command shells, cause SYN floods and manage files. A publicly available version includes a graphical interface for operators. Listed actors are APT41, EMISSARY PANDA and Leviathan. The reference list runs from 2014 to 2023.

b39c2c22572566062e6ff698103d3d291eb0f1e8.summary: Malwarebytes article (published 2021-04-19) on Fedir Hladyr, systems administrator of the FIN7 cybercrime group, sentenced in the US to 10 years in prison for his role. It links FIN7 to the Carbanak and Cobalt malware campaigns against banks and payment systems, which began with spear-phishing. It recounts the 2018 arrest of the gang leader in Spain, announced by Europol, and the 2018 arrests of three members. A 2020 cooperation with Ryuk operators is suspected. Cited losses include over EUR 1 billion and $900 million, plus 15 million stolen card records.

b31245aa28777ce928ce0325c7a77db3a42edc1a.summary: NCC Group research (published June 23, 2020) on WastedLocker, a ransomware locker first seen in use in May 2020 and attributed by the report to the Evil Corp group. The report covers Evil Corp's history with Dridex, BitPaymer and Ryuk; distribution through the SocGholish fake update framework, which delivers a custom CobaltStrike loader; privilege escalation via a UAC bypass; per-file AES encryption with RSA-wrapped keys; and anti-analysis and endpoint-evasion behaviour. Several attributions and observations are explicitly hedged by the authors.

hedges: We believe those changes were ultimately caused by the unsealing of indictments against two named individuals and the financial sanctions against Evil Corp in December 2019.
The report asserts certain Evil Corp points with high confidence, based on the authors' in-depth tracking of the group.
Business associations in cybercrime groups are fluid, so threat intelligence reporting on group composition can be misleading.
It is possible that the post-indictment inactivity was primarily a strategic move to suggest Evil Corp was still active.
It is thought that the Gozi ISFB 2 variant is intended as a replacement for Dridex botnet 501 as a persistent component.
It is assumed that the CrowdStrike-related loader logic is an attempt to bypass CrowdStrike's endpoint solution, although it is still unclear if this is the case.
It is believed that the SecTool checker tool is used during ransomware deployment, but the authors have no specific evidence that Evil Corp used it.
Other distribution methods appear to still be in use, but the authors have not been able to independently verify this at the time of writing.
